nodes.label: Self-serve signup wizard (/signup)
nodes.rationale: OTP → partial account → PAN → Business Details → PIN → /console, replacing the old Zoho lead-capture iframe. Every step re-fetches interaction 151 so resume-after-drop-off and retry-after-failure are the same code path.

nodes.label: `onboarding === 1` classification gate in getProfile
nodes.rationale: user_type flips to "23" the moment the partial account exists, so it cannot distinguish in-progress from finished. Checking user_type first would classify every mid-onboarding user as not_allowed and permanently lock them out of resuming.

nodes.label: `signup` session role
nodes.rationale: GET /me special-cases the role before any Eko call because AuthProvider boots exclusively from /me — rejecting a signup session would drop a mid-onboarding reload to anon and force a fresh OTP.

nodes.label: respond() signup→developer session upgrade
nodes.rationale: Gates on profile.kind === 'found' rather than buildMeView output, which never throws and would silently mint a developer session for exactly the profiles /auth/otp/verify refuses. A throwing re-fetch still returns done and retries on the next /signup/state.

nodes.label: Pintwin PIN encoding (170 → 10005 → 5)
nodes.rationale: Digit substitution, not encryption — the key ships in the clear, so obfuscation is all it buys alone. The real property is that each key is single-use and invalidated upstream per attempt, so a captured okekey cannot be replayed. Encoding runs entirely in the BFF.

nodes.label: Interaction 521 — createPartialAccount
nodes.rationale: Uses base() — the configured default initiator_id/user_code pair — because no real user identity exists yet, mirroring connect-api's DEFAULT_TRXN_* fallback.

nodes.label: Interaction 523 — verifyPan (multipart)
nodes.rationale: The only onboarding interaction sent as multipart: one part literally named `form-data` carrying the same URL-encoded field string, no file part. Unverified against real upstream — a UAT gate.

nodes.label: Interaction 522 — submitBusiness / BUSINESS_FIELDS
nodes.rationale: The ten field names are unverified against real upstream — every test only asserts our own assumptions back to us; a response_type_id other than 1567 with a field-specific message means a key name is wrong.

nodes.label: ekoLog redaction (first_okekey/second_okekey/pintwin_key)
nodes.rationale: The substitution is a plain digit map, so an okekey AND the pintwin_key that produced it, logged together, recover the PIN exactly — redacting both independently closes this regardless of which log line is read first. Redaction lives inside ekoLog, not at call sites.

nodes.label: INDIAN_STATES (probed from interaction 387)
nodes.rationale: Confirmed against real UAT; its quirks ("PondiCherry" casing, Delhi with a (UT) suffix, "Andhra Pradesh (New)" sorted last, no Ladakh) are load-bearing because interaction 522 matches on the exact string.

nodes.label: ONBOARDING_LATLONG constant
nodes.rationale: This flow does not port Eloka's geolocation capture; Eloka itself falls back to this exact value when capture is skipped or denied. Not confirmed against real UAT.

nodes.label: resolveSteps() + SIGNUP_STEPS registry
nodes.rationale: Step order and labels come from the API's onboarding_steps at runtime; the wizard never branches on step names and each StepDefinition owns its own submit closure. Unknown API roles are silently skipped so the backend can ship a step before the frontend has UI.

nodes.label: StepRail progress UI
nodes.rationale: One component and one DOM tree with orientation swapped in CSS only, so no second render branch can drift; holds no state and returns null rather than claiming 'Step 0 of 0'.

nodes.label: connect-api login delegation (CONNECT_API_BASE_URL)
nodes.rationale: When set, login is delegated to Eloka's connect-api so the EPS portal and Eloka share one identity; mapConnectLogin maps its envelope onto the same ProfileResult union in the same branch order. Only login is delegated.

nodes.label: No Eko access token (developer_key + initiator_id = mobile)
nodes.rationale: The Bearer token Eloka sends never goes upstream — connect-api only derives initiator_id/user_code/org_id from it. initiator_id is the registered mobile, never an internal id; sending ekoUserId earns a misleading 'Invalid Sender/Initiator' 403.

hyperedges.label: Signup onboarding interaction chain (521 → 523 → 522 → pintwin → session upgrade)
